text: A horse's blood climbed eight feet up a glass tube. Stephen Hales, a vicar, wanted to measure the push of a heartbeat. He fixed a tall tube into a mare's artery. The blood rose taller than a man, bobbing with every beat. In 1733 he published the first blood pressure reading.
